summary: Architecture: clean 4-project layered solution (Core → Infrastructure → App + Tests). Dependency direction is enforced — Core has no external deps, Infrastructure refs Core only, App refs Core + Infrastructure.
Program.cs two-phase init pattern is correct: AppPaths → EnsureDefaultSettingsFile → JsonSettingsService → Generic Host. Ordering guarantees the settings file exists before IConfiguration reads it.
JsonSettingsService uses atomic temp-file + File.Move write; corruption falls back to defaults. Both patterns are correct.
ThemeService wiring is clean: ThemeChanged event subscribed in App.axaml.cs; ApplyTheme maps ThemeMode to Avalonia ThemeVariant correctly.
Ctrl+T shortcut fully gated by #if DEBUG in both ViewModel (RelayCommand) and code-behind (KeyBinding registration). Release binary is clean.
Test coverage is appropriate for M1 scope: AppPathsTests, JsonSettingsServiceTests, LoggingVerbosityMappingTests, ThemeServiceTests all pass.

One medium-priority documentation error found: README.md verbosity table documents the scale as 1=Verbose→4=Warning (inverted) but actual code/LoggingOptions.cs comment/tests all confirm 1=Warning→4=Verbose. Raised as observation — does not block M1 acceptance criteria.

comments.note: README.md Configuration table documents Verbosity as '1=Verbose, 2=Debug, 3=Information, 4=Warning, 5=Error' — completely inverted vs the actual implementation. LoggingOptions.cs, LoggingSetup.cs, and LoggingVerbosityMappingTests all confirm 1=Warning, 2=Information, 3=Debug, 4=Verbose (no 5). The description column in the README table should read: '1=Warning, 2=Information, 3=Debug, 4=Verbose'. Non-blocking for M1 but will mislead users configuring the app.

Dual first-run init: Program.Main calls EnsureDefaultSettingsFile (writes embedded defaults to disk) AND JsonSettingsService.LoadOrInitialise has its own first-run write path. Both paths are safe (idempotent due to File.Exists guard), but the redundancy adds cognitive load. Consider removing the WriteDefaultsSync path from JsonSettingsService if EnsureDefaultSettingsFile is always called first, or remove EnsureDefaultSettingsFile and let JsonSettingsService own the full init flow.

App.Services static property uses null-forgiving assignment (= null!). This is a documented Avalonia startup pattern where ordering is deterministic, so it is acceptable here. If any future code path could access Services before Program.Main completes (e.g. design-time previewer), consider guarding with a null check or lazy initializer.
